content.text: The run finished with no unrecovered errors: 401s were handled by refreshing the token and 429s by honouring `retry_after`. One thing needs checking before I trust the numbers. The listing returned 1500 items across 30 full pages but only 1480 distinct ids, so the duplicates might be hiding missing orders. I'll dump the listing to `/tmp/recon` and check whether the ids are contiguous.

input.command:
cd /tmp/recon && cat > dump.py <<'EOF'
import json, sys
sys.argv = ["x"]
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("r", "/tmp/recon/reconcile.py")
r = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(r)
items, path, pg = [], "/orders?page=1", 0
while path:
    page = r.fetch(path); pg += 1
    items.extend(page["items"]); path = page["next"]
json.dump(items, open("/tmp/recon/listing.json", "w"))
print("pages", pg, "items", len(items))
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/recon/dump.py 2>/dev/null && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json, collections
items = json.load(open("/tmp/recon/listing.json"))
ids = [i["id"] for i in items]
nums = sorted({int(x.split("-")[1]) for x in ids})
print("distinct", len(nums), "min", nums[0], "max", nums[-1])
missing = sorted(set(range(nums[0], nums[-1]+1)) - set(nums))
print("gaps in id sequence:", len(missing), missing[:20])
c = collections.Counter(ids)
dups = [k for k,v in c.items() if v>1]
pos = {}
for idx, i in enumerate(items):
    pos.setdefault(i["id"], []).append(idx)
print("dup positions (1-based idx):", [ (k, [p+1 for p in pos[k]]) for k in dups[:20]])
print("dup at page boundary (pos 50/51 pattern):", sum(1 for k in dups if (pos[k][1]) % 50 == 0))
EOF

content.text: The ids run contiguously from ord-0001 to ord-1480 with no gaps, and every duplicate is a page-boundary repeat, so nothing was missed. Next I'll check the timestamp handling, since that's where the UTC rule is most likely to go wrong.

input.command:
cd /tmp/recon && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json, re, collections
from datetime import datetime, timezone
items = {i["id"]: i for i in json.load(open("/tmp/recon/listing.json"))}.values()
fmts = collections.Counter(re.sub(r"\d", "9", i["placed_at"]) for i in items)
print("timestamp shapes:", dict(fmts))
print("amount types:", collections.Counter(type(i["amount_cents"]).__name__ for i in items))
print("status exact values:", sorted({repr(i["status"]) for i in items}))
RS = datetime(2025,3,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc); RE = datetime(2025,6,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
near = []
for i in items:
    t = datetime.fromisoformat(i["placed_at"].replace("Z","+00:00")).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    if abs((t-RS).total_seconds()) < 86400*1.1 or abs((t-RE).total_seconds()) < 86400*1.1:
        near.append((i["placed_at"], i["status"], i["amount_cents"], "IN" if RS<=t<RE else "out"))
for n in sorted(near): print(n)
EOF

cd /tmp/recon && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json, re, collections
from datetime import datetime, timezone
items = {i["id"]: i for i in json.load(open("/tmp/recon/listing.json"))}.values()
fmts = collections.Counter(re.sub(r"\d", "9", i["placed_at"]) for i in items)
print("timestamp shapes:", dict(fmts))
print("amount types:", collections.Counter(type(i["amount_cents"]).__name__ for i in items))
print("status exact values:", sorted({repr(i["status"]) for i in items}))
RS = datetime(2025,3,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc); RE = datetime(2025,6,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
near = []
for i in items:
    t = datetime.fromisoformat(i["placed_at"].replace("Z","+00:00")).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    if abs((t-RS).total_seconds()) < 86400*1.1 or abs((t-RE).total_seconds()) < 86400*1.1:
        near.append((i["placed_at"], i["status"], i["amount_cents"], "IN" if RS<=t<RE else "out"))
for n in sorted(near): print(n)
EOF
